title: 専門教養特別科目（化学史）
subtitle: Special Subject - Specialties Education(History of Chemistry)
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn what chemistry is and why it is indispensable to society through lectures and practical training. In addition, participants will obtain a deep understanding of chemistry from the viewpoint of cultural, historical, and social perspectives. The course also considers the connections between chemistry and various fields such as engineering, architecture, psychology, and information technology.
advice: Through lectures and experiments, participants will learn about ancient Mesopotamian culture, classical ancient Greek and Roman culture, medieval European and Islamic culture, and the process of the establishment of chemistry in modern times. In this course, students do not learn the history of chemistry as knowledge, but rather through hands-on experience in dye synthesis, glass synthesis, battery production, alloy production, etc., as well as a background in chemistry.　 All participants should be sure to work on the assigned preparation work for the laboratory experiences and discussions. The grade evaluation is based on reports and oral examinations.

requiredKnowledge: Participants should have taken "Fundamentals of Chemistry" and "Fundamentals of Physics" in high school. No prior experience with chemistry experiments is required.

              In this course, students will learn what chemistry is and why it is indispensable to society through lectures and practical training. In addition, participants will obtain a deep understanding of chemistry from the viewpoint of cultural, historical, and social perspectives. The course also considers the connections between chemistry and various fields such as engineering, architecture, psychology, and information technology.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Through lectures and experiments, participants will learn about ancient Mesopotamian culture, classical ancient Greek and Roman culture, medieval European and Islamic culture, and the process of the establishment of chemistry in modern times. In this course, students do not learn the history of chemistry as knowledge, but rather through hands-on experience in dye synthesis, glass synthesis, battery production, alloy production, etc., as well as a background in chemistry.　 All participants should be sure to work on the assigned preparation work for the laboratory experiences and discussions. The grade evaluation is based on reports and oral examinations.
